extracted.intended_audience: Issuers of securities and their officers, investor-relations/public-relations personnel, corporate counsel, compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and definitions governing selective disclosure of material nonpublic information by issuers and persons acting on their behalf, including when and how public disclosure must be made and who is covered or excepted. Also explains related timing, methods of disclosure, and legal effects on antifraud and reporting status.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule regarding selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an issuer, or any person acting on its behalf, discloses any material nonpublic information regarding that issuer or its securities to any person described in paragraph (b)(1) of this section, the issuer shall make public disclosure of that information as provided in § 243.101(e): (1) Simultaneously, in the case of an intentional disclosure; and (2) Promptly, in the case of a non-intentional disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core obligation: selective disclosure to specified outside persons triggers an obligation to make the information public. The timing differs based on whether the disclosure was intentional (simultaneous public disclosure required) or non-intentional (prompt public disclosure required). See §243.101(e) for permitted public disclosure methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered recipients (scope of persons that trigger the rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (a) applies to a disclosure made to any person outside the issuer who is: (i) a broker or dealer, or a person associated with a broker or dealer; (ii) an investment adviser, an institutional investment manager that filed a Form 13F for the most recent quarter, or a person associated with either; (iii) an investment company (or a person who would be an investment company but for certain exceptions), or an affiliated person of either; or (iv) a holder of the issuer's securities under circumstances in which it is reasonably foreseeable that the person will purchase or sell the issuer's securities on the basis of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies precisely which external recipients constitute 'selective' disclosure for Regulation FD purposes, including statutory cross-references for definitions. The institutional investment manager coverage requires prior Form 13F filing. 'Affiliated person' has specified statutory meaning for investment companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (a) shall not apply to a disclosure made: (i) To a person who owes a duty of trust or confidence to the issuer (such as an attorney, investment banker, or accountant); (ii) To a person who expressly agrees to maintain the disclosed information in confidence; (iii) In connection with a securities offering registered under the Securities Act, other than certain Rule 415(a)(1)(i)-(vi) offerings, if the disclosure is by specified means (registration statement/prospectus, free writing prospectus after filing, other Section 10(b) prospectus, Rule 135 notice, Rule 134 communication, or an oral communication made in connection with the registered offering after filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits narrow categories of disclosures that do not trigger the public disclosure obligation, including confidential advisers and certain disclosures made in the course of registered offerings; enumerates permitted forms of offering-related communications. Also contains limits to prevent evasion (e.g., exceptions do not apply where offering is for purpose of evading this section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "intentional" disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A selective disclosure of material nonpublic information is “intentional” when the person making the disclosure either knows, or is reckless in not knowing, that the information he or she is communicating is both material and nonpublic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the scienter standard for treating a disclosure as intentional (knowledge or recklessness about materiality and nonpublic status). This determination affects the timing requirement (simultaneous public disclosure if intentional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "issuer" subject to Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: An “issuer” subject to this regulation is one that has a class of securities registered under Section 12 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, or is required to file reports under Section 15(d) of the Exchange Act, including any closed-end investment company, but not including any other investment company or any foreign government or foreign private issuer, as those terms are defined in Rule 405 under the Securities Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which entities are regulated by Part 243; includes closed-end funds but excludes other investment companies and certain foreign issuers per Rule 405 definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "person acting on behalf of an issuer"
rubrics_metrics.description: “Person acting on behalf of an issuer” means any senior official of the issuer (or, for closed-end funds, a senior official of the issuer's investment adviser), or any other officer, employee, or agent of an issuer who regularly communicates with any person described in §243.100(b)(1)(i),(ii), or (iii), or with holders of the issuer's securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also states that an officer, director, employee, or agent who discloses material nonpublic information in breach of a duty of trust or confidence to the issuer shall not be considered to be acting on behalf of the issuer—i.e., such breach disclosures are excluded from the definition of acting on behalf and may not trigger issuer's obligations under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "promptly" for non-intentional disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Promptly” means as soon as reasonably practicable (but in no event after the later of 24 hours or the commencement of the next day's trading on the New York Stock Exchange) after a senior official of the issuer learns that there has been a non-intentional disclosure by the issuer or person acting on behalf of the issuer of information that the senior official knows, or is reckless in not knowing, is both material and nonpublic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concrete maximum timing for required public disclosure after a non-intentional selective disclosure: no later than the later of 24 hours or the next NYSE trading day start, measured from when a senior official learns (with knowledge or recklessness) of the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure methods (Form 8-K and alternative dissemination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (e)(2), an issuer shall make the “public disclosure” of information required by §243.100(a) by furnishing to or filing with the Commission a Form 8-K (17 CFR 249.308) disclosing that information. An issuer shall be exempt from the requirement to furnish or file a Form 8-K if it instead disseminates the information through another method (or combination of methods) of disclosure that is reasonably designed to provide broad, non-exclusionary distribution of the information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the primary mechanism (Form 8-K) and permits alternative methods so long as they are reasonably designed to achieve broad, non-exclusionary public distribution (e.g., widely accessible press releases, public web postings, broadly disseminated news releases), subject to interpretation of 'reasonably designed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "senior official"
rubrics_metrics.description: “Senior official” means any director, executive officer (as defined in §240.3b-7 of this chapter), investor relations or public relations officer, or other person with similar functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies which persons' knowledge triggers timing obligations for determining when 'promptly' begins to run after a non-intentional disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities offering commencement and duration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §243.100(b)(2)(iv): Underwritten offerings commence when the issuer reaches an understanding with the broker-dealer that is to act as managing underwriter and continue until the later of the end of the period during which a dealer must deliver a prospectus or the sale of the securities (unless sooner terminated). Non-underwritten offerings commence and continue as specified depending on Rule 415(a)(1)(x) coverage, business combination treatment under Rule 165(f)(1), or filing of a registration statement—each with precise commencement and end points tied to bona fide offers, first public announcement of transaction, filing, prospectus delivery periods, or sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides detailed timing rules to determine when the offering-related exception to Regulation FD applies, with different rules for underwritten vs. non-underwritten offerings and special treatment for business combinations and other offering types.

rubrics_metrics.name: No effect on antifraud liability (Rule 10b-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: No failure to make a public disclosure required solely by §243.100 shall be deemed to be a violation of Rule 10b-5 (17 CFR 240.10b-5) under the Securities Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that failing to comply with Regulation FD alone does not automatically create liability under the general antifraud rule; separate antifraud obligations remain governed by Rule 10b-5.

rubrics_metrics.name: No effect on Exchange Act reporting status or adequacy of public information
rubrics_metrics.description: A failure to make a public disclosure required solely by §243.100 shall not affect whether: (a) For purposes of Forms S-3, S-8 and SF-3 under the Securities Act, or Form N-2 under the Securities Act and the Investment Company Act, an issuer is deemed to have filed all the material required to be filed pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Exchange Act or, where applicable, has made those filings in a timely manner; or (b) There is adequate current public information about the issuer for purposes of §230.144(c) of this chapter (Rule 144(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that a Regulation FD-only failure does not change an issuer's reporting status for certain shelf registration forms or the determination of adequate current public information for Rule 144(c); i.e., Regulation FD violations do not automatically affect these discrete reporting consequences.
